overall: Atlanta ran warmer than most model guidance on June 4, with the daily maximum reaching 82.4°F by 17:00 ET — driven by a clean, uninterrupted afternoon warming cycle aided by low dewpoints (51.8°F) and light winds. By 23:00 ET, temperatures have fallen sharply to 71.6°F and are still dropping at -1.8°F/hr, firmly confirming the peak is already in. The day ended roughly 2°F hotter than the ECMWF/NBM consensus but essentially on target with GFS.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS was the clear model winner at 82.3°F, nearly matching the observed 82.4°F max, while ECMWF (80.0°F) and NBM (80.1°F) both underforecast by approximately 2.3–2.4°F. The odd ensemble model's 81–82°F range was directionally closer to the outcome than the even model's 80–81°F range, though the actual max nudged slightly above even the odd model's top bin.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max locked in at 82.4°F since 17:00 and current temperature at 71.6°F falling at -1.8°F/hr at 23:00, the daily high is effectively an observed value — not a forecast. There is no realistic meteorological path to re-touching or exceeding 82.4°F overnight, making this a near-certain outcome. Confidence is extremely high: the TMAX for June 4 in Atlanta is 82.4°F.
